title: Wipro Falls as Brokerages Cut Targets and India’s $315 Billion IT Sector Faces AI-Driven Spending Squeeze
excerpt: Jefferies, Citi, and BofA downgrade Wipro after weak Q1 results and guidance, as the broader Indian IT sector grapples with subdued client spending and AI-driven efficiency measures.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Wipro shares fell over 2% after missing Q1 estimates and issuing weak guidance.
  • India's $315 billion IT sector faces pressure from cautious client spending and AI efficiency measures.
  • Wipro's deal wins dropped to $3.37 billion, down from $5 billion a year ago.
  • Tech Mahindra's shares rose 4.8% after beating revenue estimates and posting strong deal wins.

  • Wipro shares fell over 2% after missing Q1 estimates and issuing weak guidance, with 14 brokerages cutting price targets and Jefferies maintaining an underperform rating at Rs 150.
  • India’s $315 billion IT services sector faces persistent pressure from cautious client spending, prolonged decision-making cycles, and AI-driven efficiency measures that reduce outsourcing demand.
  • Wipro’s deal wins fell to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year earlier, with operating margins slipping to 16% from 17.3%.
  • Rival Tech Mahindra jumped 4.8% after beating revenue estimates and posting strong deal wins, highlighting a widening performance gap within the sector.

Wipro’s Disappointing Quarter

Wipro shares declined 2.3 percent on Friday after India’s fourth-largest IT services company missed quarterly earnings estimates and issued guidance that pointed to a delayed recovery. Revenue rose 10.6 percent year-over-year to Rs 24,479 crore ($2.54 billion) in the June quarter but fell short of analyst expectations of Rs 24,776 crore. Net profit edged up just 0.6 percent to Rs 3,352 crore.

The company guided for second-quarter revenue between $2.57 billion and $2.63 billion, implying a range from a 1.5 percent decline to 0.5 percent growth in constant-currency terms. Analysts had expected guidance of between a 1 percent decline and 1 percent increase.

Total deal wins for the quarter dropped sharply to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year earlier. Operating margins slipped to 16 percent from 17.3 percent in both the preceding quarter and a year ago, as salary hikes and the ramp-up of large deals weighed on profitability.

Brokerages Turn Bearish

Jefferies maintained its underperform rating and cut its target price to Rs 150 from Rs 180, calling it “another soft quarter” and warning that Wipro has struggled to deliver organic revenue growth over the past three years. The brokerage projected fiscal 2027 would be no different.

“Wipro has always had a growth problem. Even now, if you adjust for acquisitions, organic growth was about negative 2 percent quarter-on-quarter.”

— Sushovan Nayak, lead analyst, Anand Rathi Institutional Equities

Citi maintained its sell rating and lowered its target to Rs 150, describing the performance as “disappointing” with weakness across major geographies and verticals. Bank of America retained its underperform rating and cut its target to Rs 184, warning that the turnaround would take longer than expected. Fourteen brokerages in total cut their price targets, dragging the median to Rs 187 from Rs 210.

Ambit Capital and BOB Capital Markets suggested fiscal 2027 could mark Wipro’s fourth consecutive year of organic revenue decline.

Sector Under Structural Pressure

Wipro’s struggles reflect broader challenges facing India’s $315 billion IT services sector. Clients are cutting non-essential spending while using artificial intelligence to squeeze greater efficiency from existing technology investments — reducing the volume of outsourcing work that has been the foundation of Indian IT for decades.

The Americas market, which accounts for the bulk of Indian IT revenue, declined for Wipro due to client-specific issues and spending cuts in healthcare. CEO Srinivas Pallia cited these headwinds without providing specific details.

Investec called the period “another quarter of disappointment” and warned that growth remained constrained by delayed client decisions and slow execution of large deals. Wipro shares have fallen over 33 percent year-to-date, significantly underperforming the broader market.

Tech Mahindra Bucks the Trend

Not all Indian IT companies are struggling equally. Tech Mahindra shares jumped 4.8 percent after beating revenue estimates and posting strong deal wins. Analysts attributed the outperformance to strong execution in telecom deals and margin improvement, calling it potentially “one of the fastest-growing companies among its peers.” TCS and HCLTech also beat revenue expectations, helped by a depreciating rupee.

What It Means for NRI Investors

Indian IT stocks are widely held by diaspora investors and form a significant portion of India-focused mutual funds and ETFs. The sector’s year-to-date decline of nearly 23 percent on the Nifty IT index has eroded substantial value. For NRIs employed at these companies, the pressure on margins and deal wins raises questions about hiring plans and compensation trajectories in the near term.
